description: Between **1945** and **1975**, more than **80** countries gained independence. European empires are collapsing and the world map is changing.

hero.hook: In thirty years, the colonial empires collapsed and the world changed its map.

blocks.text: Between **1945** and **1975**, more than **80 countries** become independent. European empires, exhausted by war, gave in to nationalist movements and a world less tolerant of colonization.
This is not a simple change of flags. It is a global upheaval, at the heart of the Cold War. It also leaves inherited borders and economic dependencies.

The war shattered the image of invincibility of the metropolises. In **1941**, the **[[The Atlantic Charter (1941)]]**, signed by US President **Franklin D. Roosevelt** and British Prime Minister **Winston Churchill**, promised the right of people to choose their government. Churchill wants to limit this principle to Europe. African and Asian leaders seized it for their colonies.

Colonial soldiers fought for the freedom of others. Elites trained in the West return with ideas of independence. The United States and the USSR, for opposite reasons, rejected classic colonialism. The pressure becomes unbearable.
Roosevelt had to push Churchill, a supporter of the British Empire, so that the Atlantic Charter spoke of the rights of peoples.

The United Kingdom often negotiates to maintain influence via the **[[Commonwealth]]**, a club of former colonies. India and Pakistan become independent in **1947**. In Ghana, , independence leader, obtains sovereignty in **1957**: first British independence in sub-Saharan Africa. **[[Kwame Nkrumah]]**

France resisted more: Indochina until Diên Bien Phu (**1954**), then the Algerian War (**1954-1962**), which brought down the **[[Fourth Republic]]** (French regime from **1946** to **1958**). In **1960**, “year of Africa”, **14** French colonies became sovereign. In the Belgian Congo, the hasty departure leads to chaos and the assassination of, the first independent Prime Minister. Portugal held out until **1975**. **[[Patrice Lumumba]]**

In **1955**, the **[[The Bandung Conference (1955)]]**, in Indonesia, brings together **29** countries of Asia and Africa. For the first time, former colonies are speaking with one voice against colonialism and racism. They advocate non-alignment: not automatically choosing the American or Soviet camp.

The momentum quickly fades. Many states fall into a form of : domination by money, debt or technology rather than by the flag. At the United Nations, however, the South becomes the majority and imposes new subjects: development, apartheid, sovereignty. **[[Neocolonialism]]**
The term “Third World” was coined in **1952** by the French demographer **Alfred Sauvy**, by analogy with the Third Estate of **1789**.

sections.title: Bandung, and the voice of the South

blocks.text: The non-alignment was structured in Belgrade in **1961**, around the Yugoslav **Josip Broz Tito**, the Indian **Jawaharlal Nehru** and the Egyptian **Gamal Abdel Nasser**. But the Cold War draws many states into the orbit of one camp. Political independence does not guarantee economic independence.
